_comment: TEMPLATE — copied to your personal config.json on first run. Installed CLIs (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode / Antigravity) are auto-detected and added as specialist agents. config.json is machine-specific and git-ignored; THIS file is shareable and is the settings baseline everyone sees. Keys starting with _ are documentation only and are stripped at load time.
_language_comment: UI language. 'system' follows the OS locale and falls back to English.
_approvalMode_comment: 'auto' executes the operator plan directly. 'ask' holds any plan matching riskyPatterns for human approval; the plan is hashed, so an edited plan invalidates its approval.
_workingDir_comment: Default working folder. '.' means the folder opened in the app. Agents can only write here unless sandbox.mode is 'off'.
_budget_comment: Guard rails. dailyCallBudget caps total model calls per day; pollSeconds is how long the engine idles when the queue is empty.
_context_comment: Character budgets for assembled prompts. memoryCharBudget trims workspace memory from the end; teamContextCharBudget caps the team/round state handed to the operator.
_taskPromptCharBudget_comment: If your task text exceeds this (e.g. a 1000-line spec), the full text is written to .nexcode/TASK-<id>.md in the working folder and the prompt carries only a head+tail digest plus a 'read the full text from the file' marker. This keeps the strict JSON operator protocol intact and stops context from being silently truncated.
_timeout_comment: agentTimeoutSeconds is the hard ceiling for one delegation. cliSilenceTimeoutSeconds ends a delegation that produced no new output for that long — progress already recorded is preserved. Per-adapter silence limits (codex/gemini 180s, claude 240s, opencode 300s) override this where they are stricter.
_consent_comment: The engine refuses to start until autonomous operation is explicitly accepted in the app. Set by the consent dialog, never by hand.
_discovery_comment: Auto-discovered adapters you deleted. They are not recreated on the next scan.
_liveDiff_comment: Live line-level diff feeding the Live Code surface. The engine enforces a 500ms floor on the interval. Per file 256 KiB / 5000 lines, 24 MiB / 2000 files at task start, 1000 rendered lines per event. Binary and oversized files are summarized; .env, credentials and private keys are never put in an event payload.
_versioning_comment: Snapshot the working folder before agents start. 'Restore this version' brings back modified and deleted files and removes files created after the task. A redo checkpoint is taken before every restore, so undo is itself undoable. Restore is only allowed while the engine is idle.

sandbox._comment: Agent jail. 'workspace' = agents may only write inside the working folder; writes outside are blocked (no Docker or Git required). 'off' restores unrestricted behaviour. extraWritableDirs lists absolute paths outside the working folder that stay writable — useful for monorepos.

_projectContext_comment: Each working folder keeps a .nexcode/CONTEXT.md project profile. It is loaded for the operator when a task opens, so the whole codebase does not have to be re-scanned; at task end the operator REVISES the profile (it is a profile, not a changelog). false falls back to plain global memory.

notify._comment: POSTs {text,...} to the webhook when a task completes or fails. Compatible with Slack incoming webhooks. An empty URL disables notifications.

operator._comment: The operator is the technical lead: it plans, delegates and judges deliverables, but never writes code itself. Its role file is fixed to operator.md; you may edit the content, not the name.
operator._passFastPath_comment: When every assignment in a round finished and the newest review says VERDICT: PASS, skip the second operator evaluation call and deliver. Set false to force the older, more expensive evaluation path.

resilience._comment: On transient provider failures (rate limit / overload / network) the delegation is retried on the same agent with exponential backoff. On a permanent failure the work is handed to a healthy agent with the same capability. Going back to the operator and spending a fresh planning round is the last resort.

cliSettings._comment: CLI-wide model policy. Priority: explicit agent override > this value > the CLI's own default. An empty model uses the CLI account/organisation default.

claude._comment: Empty model uses your Claude Code account default. The UI lists the models your own session actually reports (via the Agent SDK initialize response) and applies the choice as `claude --model <name>`.

gemini._comment: Gemini CLI uses its own default model.

opencode._comment: Naming an explicit model skips auto-selection entirely (most reliable — copy a line from `opencode models`). Left empty, modelPreferences patterns are tried in order and the FIRST match wins; '*' is a wildcard. Provider names differ per user (yours may be opencode-go, minimax, openrouter or your own server), so no provider is hardcoded — reorder the list to put your own first. modelExclude lists providers not assumed reachable; delete a line to use your local server.

skills._comment: Only skills in the enabled list are scanned. The operator sees a task-scoped shortlist rather than the whole catalogue; the specialist reads the full guide from disk only when needed. On first run this list is filled with every bundled skill (turn them off in Settings > Skills); the scorer then surfaces only the relevant ones per task.

_agents_comment: The fixed six-agent core. 'role' is binding: it decides which assignment kinds the agent may receive (executor -> implement, reviewer -> review, planner -> plan/research, operator -> none). Discovered CLI agents are added alongside these, never in place of them. 'connection' picks the transport: api_only, cli_only, or cli_first (falls back to the API when the subscription quota window is exhausted).

security._comment: Trigger-driven, never continuous — an API key is enough. Reports only; it must not write files.
security.name: Security

qa._comment: First (cheapest) tier of the escalation chain defined under escalation.qa.
qa.name: QA · Test

devops._comment: Never touches production autonomously — every step asks for human approval.
devops.name: DevOps

escalation._comment: QA escalation chain, cheapest first. A simple task is solved at the first tier; the engine only climbs when the tier fails or reports low confidence.

quota._comment: CLI subscription quota tracking. When the rolling window is exhausted, cli_first agents fall back to the API and the switch is recorded in cost_logs with its connection_mode.

_riskyPatterns_comment: Text that marks a plan as destructive or irreversible. With approvalMode 'ask' such a plan waits for explicit human approval before it runs.
